description: Found in defk-cmr. A bitstring segment value is an i64 checked against 0..2^n-1, so a 64-bit segment cannot take a value with the top bit set (Gorilla's full-width XOR when signs differ): the kernel author splits it into two 32-bit halves (test/bitstring_test.exs gorilla kernel, docs/language.md 'The bitstring accumulator' Limits bullet). Once u64 lands (defk-wlu), a u64 value in a v::64 / v::size(n) segment should be accepted (check v < 2^n on the unsigned value) in both modes, and the split in the Gorilla test kernel and the doc bullet can go. Touch points: defk_bits_put in priv/defk_runtime.h, lower_append in lib/defk/compiler.ex, Ops.bits/2 in lib/defk/elixir_mode/ops.ex.

comments.text: From defk-9p6.16 (examples/gorilla_encode.exs): the two-32-bit-halves split is not needed for Gorilla's XOR bits today. The full 64-bit case can be written as x::64-signed (a signed 64-bit segment takes every i64 and writes its u64 pattern), and narrower windows of a pattern with the top bit set come out of a logical shift on the u64 view, bsr(band(x, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF), s)::size(k), whose value fits an i64 because s >= 1 there. Accepting u64 values in 64-bit segments would still make this read like gorilla_stream's own code (one meaningful_value::size(k) segment).

title: Accept u64 values in 64-bit bitstring segments
